query: Starting from bulk HfNbTaTiZr, whose low thermal conductivity is desirable for thermal insulation, what single intervention could further reduce its phonon thermal conductivity relative to the starting material? The hypothesis should address the limitation that phonon and electronic contributions are estimated to be similar from nearly 0 to 200 K, while the available 300–1200 K measurements concern a sample containing 1 wt.% oxygen. Specify the proposed intervention, its mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to the unchanged bulk baseline, the temperatures and material states for which the prediction applies, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a dual-porosity structure in bulk HfNbTaTiZr can further reduce its phonon thermal conductivity relative to the starting material.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the exact magnitude of thermal conductivity reduction
generation.falsification_experiment: Measure the thermal conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr with and without dual-porosity structure in the temperature range 300-1200 K.

## Abstract
AbstractPorous (Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2Zr0.2Hf0.2)C high-entropy ceramics (HEC) with a dual-porosity structure were fabricated by pressureless sintering using a mixture powder of ceramic precursor and SiO2 microspheres. The carbothermal reduction in the ceramic precursor led to the formation of pores with sizes of 0.4–3 μm, while the addition of SiO2 microspheres caused the appearance of pores with sizes of 20–50 μm. The porous HECs exhibit competitive thermal insulation (4.12–1.11 W·m−1 k−1) and extraordinary compressive strength (133.1–41.9 MPa), which can be tailored by the porosity of the ceramics. The excellent properties are ascribed to the high-entropy effects and dual-porosity structures. The severe lattice distortions in the HECs lead to low intrinsic thermal conductivity and high compressive strength. The dual-porosity structure is efficient at phonon scattering and inhabiting crack propagations, which can further improve the thermal insulation and mechanical properties of the porous HECs.Keywords: high-entropy carbides, pressureless sintering, porous ceramics, thermal conductivity, compressive strength
